body:
Flagged by AI reviewer in PR #2008.

## Problem
`docker/agents/entrypoint.sh:112-117` seeds `$dsh_home/settings.yaml` with `sed ... > "$dsh_home/settings.yaml"` but never creates `$dsh_home`. The script runs under `set -euo pipefail`, so if `DSH_HOME` points at a directory that does not exist yet (a custom `DSH_HOME` on a Nomad host volume, or a mount that failed to init), the redirect fails, the entrypoint aborts, and the organ never starts its poll loop. `lib/dsh-seed.sh` does `mkdir -p "$DSH_HOME"` before the identical write — the entrypoint should do the same. Verified locally: running the extracted block with `DSH_HOME=/tmp/x/a/b` produces `No such file or directory` on the redirect.

## Fix
Add `mkdir -p "$dsh_home" 2>/dev/null || true` (or a guarded `mkdir -p`) inside the seeding branch before the `sed` write.

---
*Auto-created from AI review*


## Affected files

- `docker/agents/entrypoint.sh` — the dsh provider-settings seeding block that writes `"$dsh_home/settings.yaml"` with no `mkdir -p "$dsh_home"` beforehand.
- `lib/dsh-seed.sh` — the reference implementation (`dsh_seed_home()`) that does `mkdir -p "$DSH_HOME"` before the identical write.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docker/agents/entrypoint.sh` creates `$dsh_home` (guarded `mkdir -p`) before the `sed ... > "$dsh_home/settings.yaml"` redirect.
- [ ] The entrypoint still starts when `DSH_HOME` points at a path that does not exist yet (e.g. `DSH_HOME=/tmp/x/a/b`).
- [ ] An existing operator-customised `settings.yaml` is still never overwritten.
- [ ] ShellCheck passes on the changed file.
- [ ] No default constants (`DSH_CONTEXT_WINDOW`, `CLAUDE_TIMEOUT`, `MAX_DIFF`, `DIFF_THRESHOLD`, `DIGEST_CAP`) move.

Flagged by AI reviewer in PR #2008.

## Problem
`docker/agents/entrypoint.sh` now seeds a missing `$DSH_HOME/settings.yaml` from `${DSH_SEED_DIR:-/opt/dsh}/settings-<DSH_PROVIDER>.yaml` (#2004), but `lib/dsh-seed.sh` — the seeding path used by `docker/runner/entrypoint-runner.sh` (vault runner) and the reproduce/triage sidecars — still hardcodes `"$seed/settings-llamacpp.yaml"` (lib/dsh-seed.sh:23) and knows nothing about `DSH_PROVIDER`. The entrypoint comment cites `lib/dsh-seed.sh` as the reference for `DSH_SEED_DIR` handling, so the two paths now diverge: a runner or sidecar with `DSH_PROVIDER=xai` silently gets the llama.cpp settings.

## Fix
Mirror the provider lookup and the `^[a-z0-9-]+$` guard in `dsh_seed_home()`, and extend `tests/acceptance/issue-1836.sh` / `issue-1837.sh` to cover the provider selection.

---
*Auto-created from AI review*


## Affected files

- `lib/dsh-seed.sh` — `dsh_seed_home()` hardcodes `"$seed/settings-llamacpp.yaml"` (line 23).
- `docker/agents/entrypoint.sh` — the provider-aware seeding to mirror (`DSH_PROVIDER` + `^[a-z0-9-]+$` guard).
- `tests/acceptance/issue-1836.sh`, `tests/acceptance/issue-1837.sh` — extend for provider selection.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `dsh_seed_home()` selects `${DSH_SEED_DIR:-/opt/dsh}/settings-$DSH_PROVIDER.yaml`, defaulting to `llamacpp` when `DSH_PROVIDER` is unset.
- [ ] The provider name is validated with the same `^[a-z0-9-]+$` guard as `docker/agents/entrypoint.sh`.
- [ ] A missing or invalid provider template warns on stderr and seeds nothing (no silent llama.cpp fallback).
- [ ] The acceptance tests cover both the default `llamacpp` provider and a named provider.
- [ ] `mkdir -p "$DSH_HOME"` still runs before the `sed ... > "$DSH_HOME/settings.yaml"` write.
- [ ] ShellCheck passes on the changed files.
